title: AFRICOM Discloses Third Strike Near Kismayo, Pushing 2026 Somalia Total Past 81
detail: US Africa Command publicly confirmed on September 11, 2026 that it struck Al-Shabaab near Quumbi, approximately 50 miles (80 km) northwest of Kismayo, on September 8 — its third disclosed Somalia strike within a week, following the September 4 strike west of Mogadishu and a September 5 strike also near Quumbi. The disclosure brings the confirmed 2026 US airstrike total in Somalia to at least 81, keeping the year on pace to approach or exceed 2025's record of roughly 124-126 strikes. As with the prior strikes, AFRICOM withheld unit, aircraft, weapons and casualty details, citing operational security, and said the strike was conducted in coordination with the Federal Government of Somalia.

title: Pirates Release Cargo Ship Sward Near Garacad After Ransom Paid
detail: Somali pirates released the St Kitts-flagged cargo vessel Sward near Garacad, Puntland, around September 11, 2026, after a ransom was paid, according to security sources. The Sward was hijacked approximately 6 nautical miles northeast of Garacad on April 26, 2026, with a crew of 17 (15 Syrian and 2 Indian nationals) held hostage for over four months. Security sources said the pirates had used the Sward as a mothership to help capture at least two additional vessels during its captivity before departing by vehicle onshore; the crew remained aboard. The exact ransom amount was not disclosed, though comparable 2026 payments have ranged from roughly $2.5M (MV Lutuf) to reported demands as high as $10M (MT Eureka). The release marks the first resolution among the roughly half-dozen vessels seized in Somalia's 2026 piracy resurgence.

media.caption: The cargo vessel Sward was released near Garacad after a ransom was paid, ending a four-month hijacking
